policy_name: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
geo_constraints: Addressed to UNESCO Member States, and through them to AI actors

key_dates.event: Adopted by the UNESCO General Conference at its 41st session

version: SHS/BIO/PI/2021/1 (document code from general knowledge; not verified)
covered_entities: AI actors (incl. researchers, developers, deployers, companies, users)
covered_systems: AI systems (broadly understood as systems with the capacity to process data in a way resembling intelligent behaviour)
covered_activities: entire AI system lifecycle: research, design, development, deployment, use, maintenance, termination
conditions: non-binding; Member States invited to apply via legislative or other measures and report periodically
objective: Provide a universal framework of values, principles and policy actions to guide States in ensuring that AI systems work for the good of humanity, individuals, societies and the environment and prevent harm.
principles: right to privacy and data protection

related_policies.policy: UNESCO Readiness Assessment Methodology and Ethical Impact Assessment tool

conflict_rule: Non-binding; to be applied consistent with international human rights law and Member States' constitutional practice.

Clause texts are paraphrases/reconstructions, not verbatim.

clauses.section: Section III.2 Principles - Proportionality and Do No Harm
clauses.original_text: The choice to use AI systems and which AI method to use should be justified: the method should be appropriate and proportional to achieve a legitimate aim, should not infringe human rights, and should be appropriate to the context. Where decisions may have irreversible or difficult-to-reverse impacts or involve life and death, final human determination should apply. AI systems in particular should not be used for social scoring or mass surveillance purposes.
clauses.requirement: use AI only where proportionate to a legitimate aim; not for social scoring or mass surveillance

clauses.section: Section III.2 Principles - Human oversight and determination
clauses.original_text: Member States should ensure that it is always possible to attribute ethical and legal responsibility for any stage of the life cycle of AI systems, as well as in cases of remedy related to AI systems, to physical persons or to existing legal entities. … An AI system can never replace ultimate human responsibility and accountability.
clauses.requirement: ensure responsibility for AI is always attributable to natural or legal persons; humans retain ultimate responsibility

clauses.section: Section III.2 Principles - Fairness and non-discrimination
clauses.original_text: AI actors should promote social justice and safeguard fairness and non-discrimination of any kind, and should make all reasonable efforts to minimize and avoid reinforcing or perpetuating discriminatory or biased applications and outcomes throughout the life cycle of AI systems, to ensure fairness of such systems.
clauses.object: discriminatory or biased applications and outcomes
clauses.requirement: make reasonable efforts to avoid biased or discriminatory outcomes across the lifecycle
clauses.affected_asset: equal treatment of individuals and groups

clauses.section: Section IV Policy Area 1 - Ethical Impact Assessment
clauses.original_text: Member States should introduce frameworks for impact assessments, such as ethical impact assessments, to identify and assess benefits, concerns and risks of AI systems, as well as appropriate risk prevention, mitigation and monitoring measures, among other assurance mechanisms.
clauses.requirement: establish impact assessment frameworks identifying benefits, risks and mitigation/monitoring measures

clauses.section: Section III.2 Principles - Right to Privacy and Data Protection
clauses.original_text: Privacy, a right essential to the protection of human dignity, human autonomy and human agency, must be respected, protected and promoted throughout the life cycle of AI systems. It is important that data for AI systems be collected, used, shared, archived and deleted in ways that are consistent with international law and in line with the values and principles set forth in this Recommendation.
clauses.requirement: handle data for AI consistent with international law and the Recommendation's values
